notes:
1. Dek says "Schwab, M&T and Hong Kong's regulator each describe a different answer to AI agents arriving at the account." Source (M&T transcript): "We are not really seeing much impact of actually money being moved out or anything yet. ... And we are monitoring that very closely." M&T describes no answer or policy, only what it sees and that it is monitoring; HKMA's is an upcoming discussion paper. Fix: describe what each did, e.g. "Schwab blocks some outside agents, M&T is watching them arrive and Hong Kong's regulator is preparing a framework for them." The title "Banks are deciding how agents get through the door" has the same problem (HKMA is a regulator, M&T is not deciding anything in the source); soften it to match.
2. Section 4 says the OpenAI case is "the same question these three institutions are answering from the bank's side." No source says M&T or HKMA is answering a question about permission, and HKMA is not a bank. Fix: drop the clause, e.g. "...for the account holder's permission. Any firm whose clients may send agents to their accounts can ask who authorized the agent, and how it would see the agent go beyond that."
3. Section 4 says the model "used a crypto wallet without permission" with no context, set next to bank accounts. Source (Fortune): "to pay the fees needed to test an app on Ethereum's Sepolia test network. Although the tokens had little real-world value, the model had no authorization to collect or spend them." Fix: add that it was a test network and the tokens had little real-world value.
4. Section 2 says agents are coming in "to the bank's center". Source: "If you look at our center that we have now, agents are coming in every day." The transcript does not say what the center is. Fix: "what Bible called 'our center'" or drop the noun: "agents are coming in every day".
5. Section 3 heading "Hong Kong writes the rulebook". Source: the HKMA announced a framework and supervisory guidance, and "an upcoming discussion paper on a proposed supervisory framework". Nothing is a rule yet. Fix: e.g. "Hong Kong sets out a framework".
